scope: Post-freeze public-release review findings for Manager 4.17.10

defects.title: Registry-mode UpdateHub reports pending CANDIDATE state from the global inbox instead of the active instance inbox
defects.defect_class: instance-owned pending-state reachability / completion reporting context mismatch
defects.preconditions: Multi-Hub registry is active; the captured active instance inbox contains one or more Hub CANDIDATE ZIPs; no installable APPROVED Hub package is present; the Manager-global inbox does not contain those instance-owned candidates.
defects.bad_behavior: Invoke-Update performs Hub discovery through the active instance-scoped $HubInbox, but its final no-install branch counts pending CANDIDATE ZIPs from Manager-global $Inbox. A registry-active UpdateHub can therefore print the green 'Hub remains unchanged' result instead of surfacing pending Chat Manager work that is present in the intended instance inbox.
defects.root_cause: The update completion/reporting path retained the pre-registry global inbox variable after Hub package discovery was moved to instance-scoped routing. Existing convergence coverage proved per-instance discovery/install behavior but did not execute the CANDIDATE-only no-install outcome and assert the user-visible pending-state result.

defects.title: Managed release instructions retain stale 4.17.7 qualification identities in Manager 4.17.10
defects.defect_class: managed operator documentation / release identity drift
defects.preconditions: An operator follows the managed manager/README_FIRST.md Update compatibility or Release gate sections for Manager 4.17.10 qualification/release work.
defects.bad_behavior: Normative release instructions identify Manager 4.17.7 and transition 4.17.6 -> 4.17.7, including the release-gate regression/transition description, instead of the actual Manager 4.17.9 -> 4.17.10 release path. This can direct qualification toward the wrong predecessor/version boundary.
defects.root_cause: Current-version markers were updated during successive corrective releases, but version-bound normative qualification prose was not included in the release-identity consistency checks before freeze.
